pr.title: Simplify trivial constants in SimplifyConstCondition
pr.author: dianqk

processing.reason: The PR is a semantics-preserving optimization refinement, not a value-miscompilation bug. The historical SimplifyConstCondition only matched direct `Operand::Constant` operands, so patterns like `_x = const false; assume(copy _x)` / `switchInt(move _x)` / `assert(copy _x)` were left as real control flow; the new AfterInstSimplify instance folds those adjacent-place constants to `Unreachable`/`Goto`. In every defined case this reaches exactly the same target as the old unsimplified control flow: `assume(true)` is a NOP, `assume(false)` is UB (so there is no defined execution to compare and Miri must reject it), a constant `SwitchInt` dispatches to the same `targets.target_for_value(c)`, and `Assert` folds only when `c == expected`, where the old assert would also fall through to `target` without panicking. The paired GVN change is likewise only a precision improvement: replacing the old SwitchInt/Goto whitelist with `TerminatorKind::can_write_to_memory` means derefs are invalidated exactly for Call/Drop/TailCall/Yield/InlineAsm (which may write memory) and additionally preserved for non-writing terminators; the old code invalidated extra, semantically irrelevant derefs, while both versions invalidate whenever memory could actually be written. The frozen analysis itself states this was "an incomplete optimization, not an unsound value rewrite" and that "neither statement claims the old code produced a wrong runtime value." Consequently no source-grounded original/transformed function pair can produce different defined results while faithfully encoding this historical change; fabricating one would require an unrelated value rewrite.

analysis.summary: SimplifyConstCondition gained an `AfterInstSimplify` instance and now looks through a condition that is a `copy`/`move` of a place assigned a constant in the immediately preceding statement. It folds `assume(false)` to `Unreachable`, a constant `SwitchInt` to `Goto`, and a constant `Assert` matching `expected` to `Goto`. A related GVN change replaces the hard-coded SwitchInt/Goto deref-preservation whitelist with `TerminatorKind::can_write_to_memory`, invalidating derefs only for terminators that can write memory, with `Yield` explicitly treated as writing `resume_arg`.
analysis.originalLogic: Before this patch, SimplifyConstCondition matched only direct `Operand::Constant` operands in `assume`, `SwitchInt`, and `Assert`. It did not use a preceding `_x = const C` assignment, so `assume(copy _x)` / `switchInt(move _x)` / `assert(copy _x)` stayed unsimplified even when `_x` had just been assigned a constant. GVN's old logic preserved derefs only for `SwitchInt` and `Goto`, invalidating for every other terminator because function calls and ASM may write memory.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was an incomplete optimization, not an unsound value rewrite. SimplifyConstCondition left `_x = const false; assume(copy _x); Call(precondition_check);` and `_x = const false; switchInt(move _x)` as real control flow instead of rewriting the assume block to `Unreachable` and the switch to `Goto`; the corrected pass performs those rewrites, and also folds `Assert` to `Goto` when the evaluated constant equals `expected`. GVN historically over-invalidated derefs for all non-SwitchInt/Goto terminators; the corrected GVN preserves them unless `can_write_to_memory()` is true. Neither statement claims the old code produced a wrong runtime value.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR basic blocks where a statement `Place = const C` immediately precedes an `assume(copy/move Place)`, `SwitchInt { discr: copy/move Place }`, or `Assert { cond: copy/move Place }`, with no intervening statement. The constant must successfully evaluate via `try_eval_bool` for assume/assert or `try_eval_bits` for SwitchInt. The optimization is especially relevant after `InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg` with `-Zub_checks=false` and inlining, which leaves precondition checks such as `_13 = const false; assume(copy _13); _12 = unreachable_unchecked::precondition_check()`. For GVN, the domain is all terminators, partitioned by whether they can write memory.
analysis.trigger: `-Zub_checks=false` plus `InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg`/inlining produces a block with `_13 = const false; assume(copy _13); _12 = unreachable_unchecked::precondition_check()`. The assume/switch/assert operand is a `copy`/`move` of a place just assigned a constant rather than a literal `Operand::Constant`. For GVN, the trigger is any terminator outside the old SwitchInt/Goto whitelist; deref reuse is safe only when that terminator cannot write memory.
preconditions: The constant assignment and the assume/switchInt/assert must be adjacent statements in the same basic block; SimplifyConstCondition takes/clears `pre_place_const` at every statement.
The operand must be either a direct `Operand::Constant`, or `Operand::Copy(place)`/`Operand::Move(place)` whose `Place` exactly equals the previous assignment LHS.
The constant must evaluate: `try_eval_bool` for assume/assert, `try_eval_bits` for SwitchInt.
`assume(false)` becomes `Unreachable`; `assume(true)` is a NOP; `Assert` folds only when its constant condition equals `expected`; SwitchInt uses `targets.target_for_value`.
The new instance must run after `InstSimplify::AfterSimplifyCfg`; it invalidates CFG caches.

GVN's `can_write_to_memory` must classify Call, Drop, TailCall, Yield, and InlineAsm as writing; Yield writes to `resume_arg`. Goto, SwitchInt, UnwindResume, UnwindTerminate, Return, Assert, CoroutineDrop, FalseEdge, FalseUnwind, and Unreachable do not write memory.
pitfalls: Do not generalize this to arbitrary constant propagation: only the immediately preceding `lhs = const` assignment is considered, and any intervening statement (including storage or another assignment) breaks the match.
Do not simplify `assume(false)` by merely deleting it; it denotes UB and the block should become `unreachable`.
`SwitchInt` uses bit evaluation, while `Assert` folds only on equality with `expected`; a mismatching constant assert is not rewritten to Goto.
For GVN, misclassifying a memory-writing terminator as non-writing would permit stale nested-deref reuse; Yield must be treated as writing because of `resume_arg`.

Deleting/moving the old `SimplifyConstCondition-after-const-prop` expectation is not evidence that the replacement pass is wrong; the decoded revisions show the same constant-false branch becoming `goto -> bb2`.
MIR-dump tests depend on the exact `test-mir-pass` name and `-Z` flags; the new rename is `SimplifyConstCondition-after-inst-simplify`.
analysis.testStrategy: Use MIR optimization tests rather than runtime execution. For the new pass, add `//@ test-mir-pass: SimplifyConstCondition-after-inst-simplify` with `//@ compile-flags: -Zmir-enable-passes=+InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg -Zub_checks=false -Zinline-mir` and `#![crate_type = "lib"]`; emit MIR and CHECK that the false-assume block is `unreachable;` (as in `trivial_const`). Test a materialized boolean branch such as `_1 = const false; switchInt(move _1)` becomes `goto -> bb2` (as in `simplify_if`), and the updated `control_flow_simplification` checks `bb0` is followed by `return`. For GVN, compile with `-O`, emit GVN and PreCodegen, and CHECK commoned derefs: `[[DEREF_V:_.*]] = copy (*_1);`, then `[[V1V2:_.*]] = copy (([[DEREF_V]] as Some).0: i32);`, and `_0 = Add(copy [[V1V2]], copy [[V1V2]]);` in `two_unwrap_unchecked`. A paired differential MIR test should vary only whether the condition is a direct constant or a `copy`/`move` of an immediately preceding const assignment: the corrected pass folds both, while the historical pass only folded the direct form. Exercise panic-abort/unwind variants where relevant. No compiler execution or reproduction is claimed here.

Simplifying them to unreachable early should make CFG simpler.
